title: Dedicated Cluster Sidecar: Compact Control Rail for Capacity & Burst
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
Design a compact, right-rail sidecar within the Redwood Console dedicated cluster view that surfaces an at-a-glance health & control panel for a single reserved pool. The sidecar is intended for platform engineers and SREs who need fast access to autoscale knobs, burst credits, cost impact, and a preflight simulator without leaving the cluster detail page.

Goals:
- Provide a compact controls surface that avoids modal drilling while giving safe, reversible controls for autoscale and burst.
- Surface live SLO signals (p95 latency, availability), current utilization, and burst credit balance in one glance.
- Include a lightweight cost-explain (estimated $/hr and per-token) tied to current config and a sandboxed simulator to preview changes.
- Offer clear guardrails: approval requirement for changes that exceed reserve thresholds, and an undo/rollback action for recent adjustments.

Primary users:
- Platform engineers managing dedicated pools
- App SREs troubleshooting latency or cost regressions during incidents
- Capacity planners validating burst policy changes

Proposed components and behaviors:
1) Compact header: pool name, region, tier badge, small health dot (green/amber/red) with hover tooltip linking to full pool health page.
2) Live metrics snapline: micro-sparklines for p95 latency and GPU utilization for the last 15 minutes. Numeric badges for current p95, avg utilization, error rate.
3) Autoscale quick-toggle + slider: toggle between Manual / Autoscale / Conservative Autoscale; slider to set target utilization (e.g., 60-95) with real-time estimated throughput. Slider shows hysteresis labels and recommended defaults.
4) Burst bank card: current credits, burn rate, typical recovery time. Action button "Allocate Burst" that opens a confined inline confirm panel.
5) Cost impact preview: small breakdown of token cost, GPU amortized cost per hour, and projected delta if the proposed change is applied. Link to the cost breakdown page for deep dive.
6) Preflight simulator: sandbox run that uses recent 24h traffic traces to simulate latency and cost under proposed settings. Results presented as delta bars (latency, spend). Simulator is non-blocking and uses cached traces to avoid infra load.
7) Change history & quick rollback: last three changes with a timestamp and a one-click revert in case of misconfiguration.
8) Safety rules + approval hints: show if change requires approval (e.g., plan > 2x capacity or cost delta > 30%).

Accessibility & responsiveness:
- Compact rail collapses to an icon strip on narrow screens; expanded mode remains keyboard-accessible.
- All interactive controls follow 4.5:1 contrast, focus ring, and ARIA labels.

Acceptance criteria:
- Hi-fi Figma screens for collapsed/expanded states, desktop + tablet.
- Interactive prototype (Figma or InVision) demonstrating slider, burst allocation flow, and preflight simulation with sample data.
- Engineering handoff doc with component specs (tokens, colors, thresholds) and a list of telemetry events to emit.
- Usability test notes from two platform engineers and one SRE.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Simulator accuracy vs infra cost: we choose cached trace simulation to limit infra while accepting approximate results.
- Density of controls: condensed rail risks clutter—we prioritize progressive disclosure and tooltips.
- Permissions complexity: some teams need RBAC gating; propose showing disabled controls with reason & link to request flow.

Links and artifacts:
- PRD: https://confluence.company/redwood/dedicated-console-sidecar (mock link)
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/dedicated-sidecar-v1 (prototype)
- Prototype (video): https://drive.google.com/file/d/sidecar-demo
- Example telemetry spec: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/telemetry-sidecar

Notes on uniqueness vs other designs:
This ticket intentionally focuses on a sidecar "control rail" pattern (inline, per-pool) rather than a full-screen dashboard. Emphasis is on rapid safe control, cost preview, and a sandboxed simulator which differs from earlier large dashboards that prioritize broad observability.

decisions: Use cached trace simulator to balance infra cost and UX speed
Expose a compact autoscale toggle with three presets: Manual / Conservative / Aggressive
Require approval for changes that multiply reserved capacity by 2x or increase cost >30%
